details.suggestions: The agent correctly pulled oti/oti_a/oti_t/ati for Transformer 1 at MAIN, identified only 5 samples, and correctly applied the fallback rule (foundation model context length 96 > available history), reporting the naive baseline backtest (pred 86 vs actual 85, error 1°C) and the 1-step forecast of 85°C, which are arithmetically consistent with the retrieved data. However, the tool sequence deviates from expected behavior: it did not call iot.stream_extent to confirm the data window, did not use tsfm.profile_series to check series length, and used tsfm.search_models with a free-text 'chronos' query (which returned nothing) instead of tsfm.find_models with task_id tsfm_forecasting. The visible trace also does not show a tsfm.run_recipe call for the naive baseline or the model card lookup that established the 96-sample context requirement, so those claims should be backed by explicit tool outputs. The agent should also have explicitly attempted to run the foundation model (or shown the resolve_model/find_models output) to justify the 'insufficient context' determination rather than asserting it. The alarm-proximity reasoning is acceptable given oti_a/oti_t appear to be indicator flags rather than thresholds, but the agent could have stated the numeric distances (forecast and latest reading are identical at 85, so proximity is unchanged) more directly.

task_choices: omitted / anything else  - FORECASTING: transforms -> single|ensemble -> conformal
tsfm_anomaly_detection   - detector path, producing dense anomaly labels
estimator_spec: model_id     - a catalog card, e.g. {"model_id": "ttm_r1_512_96"}; its sktime_class and params are read from the card (see find_models / resolve_model)
sktime_class - an inline class path + params, e.g. {"sktime_class": "sktime.forecasting.naive.NaiveForecaster", "params": {"strategy": "drift"}}
optional_blocks: transforms - list of transform specs applied to the target before the forecaster
ensemble   - {"members": [<estimator spec>, ...], "combine": "mean|median|min|max|weighted|stack", "weights": [...]} - use INSTEAD of estimator
finetune   - training block; see param_hints (lr, epochs, batch_size, ...)
save_to    - directory path; after a fine-tune, persist the fitted weights there and return checkpoint_path in the result (feed it to register_finetuned)
eval       - {"metrics": ["smape", ...]} - the first metric scores the backtest
rules: a recipe MUST carry an `estimator` or an `ensemble` (not both)
`model_id` must exist in the catalog; run_recipe errors if it does not
run_tabular_recipe extracts FLOps features first, then fits `estimator`; omit label_column for clustering
the series itself is never in the recipe - it arrives via dataset_path
